DECL	{"assumptions":[],"binders":["v"],"id":"NRS_484A_450_2","intentions":[],"laws":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"narrowings":[{"kind":"reading","span":"s3","why":"The record bounds the search for the halt by the mark's stopping zone (off the mark, short of it, farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance) and leaves the third place — the point at which the view of s4 is met — without a zone for the search to end at. The zone of that place is read as the stretch of the carrier, outside the junction, on which that view is met: the search back from the entry ends at the last observation at which the vehicle was on the carrier, outside the junction, and the view was not met. Nothing else ends it, as with a mark."},{"kind":"reading","span":"s3","why":"st.lane_direction, which the record claims beside prim.region_offset_along for the side of the mark, is read on its own as the carrier carrying a designated direction at the observation judged: the magnitude of the direction a formula reads (normalised, so at least one) is above zero exactly where the source records one, and is unknown where it records none. The place of the halt is read only where that direction is recorded, since the side of the mark is read along it."},{"kind":"reading","span":"s3","why":"“the carrier the vehicle approaches through” is written as every carrier the vehicle occupies whose entrance end is the junction entered and which the stop sign governs: the duty must be met through each of them, as st.lane_enters directs (“a rule never picks the carrier that favours the road user”). Where the vehicle occupies one such carrier, the ordinary case, this reading and a reading that picks one agree."}],"operationalizations":[{"concepts":["rel.occupies","rel.visible","st.highway","st.intersection","st.on_way","st.sight_along_way","st.travel_region"],"params":["p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"standard":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","surrogate":false}],"residues":[],"surrogate":false}
